description:
Return a browser page where the user uploads their own finished files
(PDF, EPS, images, ZIP) for the products in the cart — one upload slot per line.

Use when the user already has finished artwork and doesn't need a
design from us (for a design, use `design_generate_candidates` instead; a
line needs one or the other before payment). Do NOT ask for a local
file path and do NOT claim you cannot accept files.

Quote the cart first and pass the offer the customer chose for each line in
`offer_ids`, one per line; a line with no chosen offer fails with
`OfferChoiceRequiredError`. Every line in the cart gets an upload slot, and a
product added later needs its own checkout link. If `catalog_configure_product`
reported an Unmet Constraint for a line, the call fails with
`UnmetConstraintUnansweredError` until the customer answers; if they accept the
line as configured, call again with `unmet_accepted=true`. Pass `order_id` only
for an order that already had a payment link.

Unless the host gave you a file reference for the artwork, put the returned
`url` in your reply as a markdown hyperlink (never the raw URL). When the
upload card is displayed, it shows an "Open upload page" button wired to the
`url`, so just confirm the upload page is ready and share the `url` again
only if the customer asks for it. Returns a job — poll until
SUCCEEDED.
name: order_get_artwork_upload_page

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Get the artwork upload page
